items.title: Curator calls surfaced by the #699 review: Na2-citrate on trisodium citrate, Tricine on a grouping class, ledgers that can re-propose retired names
items.body:
Three findings from reviewers on #699 that need a ruling rather than a rule, filed together because each is small.

**1. `Na2-citrate` is an `EXACT_SYNONYM` on the Trisodium citrate record.** By nomenclature Na2-citrate is *disodium hydrogen* citrate, a different salt from Na3. #699's test cannot see it: that test fires when ChEBI assigns the name to another term, and this ChEBI build has no disodium citrate term at all. The 2026-04-19 `audit_mim_merge` absorbed `Na2-citrate.yaml` *and* `Citric_Acid_2.yaml` / `Citric_Acid_3.yaml` into the trisodium record — so the merge itself conflated an acid and two salts, and summed their occurrence counts. #699 retires `Citric Acid` there; whether recipe rows whose raw label is "Citric Acid" or "Na2-citrate" still count toward this record's 182 occurrences was not checked.

**2. The Tricine record maps to a structureless grouping class.** `Tricine.yaml` → `CHEBI:46760 tricine`, which in this build has a label and nothing else: no formula, no InChIKey, no definition. Its children are `CHEBI:39063` (the neutral form, which owns the structure and the systematic names) and `CHEBI:46759` (the zwitterion). Section 3 asks for the most specific stable identifier; CHEBI:39063 looks like it, and the three tricine names #699 retired from *Lithocholic acid* would be legitimate synonyms there. The record has CAS 5704-04-1 and 44 occurrences.

**3. Two tracked review ledgers still list the cadmium names against calcium nitrate.** `mappings/ingredient_mappings_synonym_enrich_review.tsv` (line 98, `ALREADY_REPRESENTED`) and `mappings/ingredient_mappings_oak_ols_review.tsv` (line 441, verdict `SYNONYM_ENRICH`). They are historical artifacts and probably how the names got in. The backfill is safe — it treats a `REJECTED_LABEL` entry as already present — but a re-run of *that enrichment* reading these ledgers could re-propose them. Either regenerate the ledgers or have the enrichment honour `REJECTED_LABEL`.

Smaller, same records: several carry a stale first `evidence` entry (`DATABASE_MATCH`, "quality=DIRECT_MATCH") that was produced for the original *wrong* mapping and now sits under the corrected `ontology_id`, reading as database support for a mapping it never supported.

items.title: 33 unified rows (3,378 recipe occurrences) lost their identity: nine merge tombstones no longer resolve to their merge target
items.body:
`UNIFIED_INGREDIENT_MAPPING.tsv` on `main` (1742bfd4) has 33 rows that are REJECTED with an empty `chebi_id`, `kg_microbe_node_id` and `mim_id`. They cover 3,378 recipe occurrences, and all 33 were MAPPED at 48408270 (#731, 2026-09-22).

| snapshot | REJECTED rows with no identity | occurrences |
|---|---:|---:|
| 48408270 (#731, 2026-09-22) | 0 | 0 |
| a8b26f00 (#754, 2026-09-25) | 47 | 9,386 |
| 6643131b (#802, 2026-10-05) | 47 | 9,391 |
| 1742bfd4 (#863, 2026-10-12) | 33 | 3,378 |

kg-microbe's consolidator skips REJECTED rows (`scripts/consolidate_chemical_mappings.py:1604-1606` at kg-microbe 1408e7099). MIM therefore supplies no identity for these labels. I did not check what kg-microbe falls back to.

## Cause

claw's unified builder finds a merge tombstone's target in `_mim_merge_target` (`scripts/build_unified_ingredient_mapping.py:129-140` at the pinned claw a5d56296):

```python
for event in reversed(data.get('curation_history', []) or []):
    if event.get('action') in MIM_MERGE_ACTIONS:
        return (data.get('identifier') or '').strip()
    if event.get('new_status') == 'REJECTED':
        return ''
```

The builder walks the history backwards and stops at the first event with `new_status: REJECTED`. Nine tombstones later gained a bookkeeping event recorded as REJECTED → REJECTED, so the walk stops before it reaches the merge:

| tombstone | identifier | blocking event |
|---|---|---|
| `Cocl2_X_6_H2o` | CHEBI:53503 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Na2moo42h2o` | CHEBI:75213 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Calcium_Chloride` | CHEBI:3312 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Sodium_Citrate` | CHEBI:32142 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Trisodium_Citrate_X_2_H2o` | CHEBI:32142 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Na-glutamate` | CHEBI:64243 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Mgcl2x_6_H2o` | CHEBI:86345 | CORRECTED (#739) |
| `Nah2po4h2o` | CHEBI:114249 | CORRECTED (#755) |
| `Cinnamic_Acid` | CHEBI:35697 | CORRECTED (#755); none of the 33 rows |

The corpus has 81 REJECTED records. Of these, 13 set `representative:`, 51 resolve through their merge event, these 9 resolve to nothing, and 8 have no merge event. The #755 CORRECTED events were written "so the merged name is credited to the live record". In the unified build they have the opposite effect.

## Rows affected

| labels | occurrences | identity at 48408270 | answer the records support now |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `CoCl2 x 6 H2O` | 2,317 | CHEBI:53503 cobalt chloride hexahydrate | same |
| 7 other CoCl2·6H2O spellings | 358 | CHEBI:35696 cobalt dichloride (anhydrous) | CHEBI:53503 |
| 6 Na2MoO4·2H2O spellings | 412 | CHEBI:75213 sodium molybdate dihydrate | same |
| 5 Na2MoO4·H2O spellings | 8 | CHEBI:75215 sodium molybdate (anhydrous) | none: no monohydrate record |
| `Sodium citrate`, `Sodium Citrate`, `sodium citrate` | 94 | CHEBI:53258 sodium citrate | contested, see below |
| `Calcium chloride`, `calcium chloride` | 82 | CHEBI:86158 calcium chloride dihydrate | CHEBI:3312 (live `CaCl2` lists `Calcium chloride`) |
| `Calcium Chloride` | 15 | CHEBI:3312 calcium dichloride | same |
| `Trisodium citrate x 2 H2O`, `Trisodium citrate・2H2O` | 77 | CHEBI:53258 sodium citrate | CHEBI:32142 sodium citrate dihydrate |
| `Trisodium citrate・3H2O`, `Trisodium citrate x 3 H2O` | 3 | CHEBI:53258 | none: no record for that form |
| `NaH2PO4•H2O` | 4 | CHEBI:37585 sodium dihydrogenphosphate (anhydrous) | CHEBI:114249 monohydrate |
| `MgCl2x 6 H2O` | 4 | CHEBI:86345 magnesium dichloride hexahydrate | same |
| `MgCl2 x 7H2O` | 2 | CHEBI:6636 magnesium dichloride (anhydrous) | kgmicrobe.compound:mgcl2_x_7_h2o |
| `Na-glutamate` | 2 | CHEBI:64220 monosodium glutamate | CHEBI:64243 monosodium L-glutamate |

- **Rows that lost an identity the records still support:** 2,748 occurrences in the "same" rows, mostly `CoCl2 x 6 H2O` (2,317) and the sodium molybdate dihydrate spellings (412).
- **Rows that had a wrong form at 48408270:** 534 occurrences. These should have been corrected, not dropped.
- **Contested labels (94 occurrences):** for the sodium citrate names, live `Trisodium citrate` (CHEBI:53258) lists `Sodium citrate`, while live `Na3-citrate x 2 H2O` (CHEBI:32142, the dihydrate) lists `Sodium Citrate`.
- **`Na-glutamate` (2 occurrences):** it had generic monosodium glutamate, where MIM now holds the L-form.

## Fix

Setting `representative:` on the nine tombstones, as 13 others already do, would make claw resolve them again. That step alone is not safe. Several tombstones still carry names of other forms as publishable synonyms, and a restored merge target would publish those names under the wrong form:

- `Cocl2_X_6_H2o` (hexahydrate): `CoCl2 x 2 H2O` and `CoCl2 x 4 H2O` (HYDRATE_FORM). Both forms have had their own records since #863.
- `Na2moo42h2o` (dihydrate): four monohydrate spellings (HYDRATE_FORM): `Na2MoO4 . H2O`, `Na2MoO4 · H2O`, `Na2MoO4.H2O` and `Na2MoO4xH2O`.
- `Mgcl2x_6_H2o` (hexahydrate): five spellings, `MgCl2 x 7 H2O`, `MgCl2 x 7H2O`, `MgCl2x7H2O`, `MgCl2  x 7 H2O` and `MgCl2  x 76 H2O` (HYDRATE_FORM).
- `Trisodium_Citrate_X_2_H2o` (dihydrate): `Trisodium citrate·3H2O` (HYDRATE_FORM).
- `Calcium_Chloride` (anhydrous): `CaCl22H2O` (HYDRATE_FORM). #757 retyped two other dihydrate spellings but not this one.
- `Na-glutamate` (monosodium L-glutamate): `(2S)-2-aminopentanedioate` and `L-glutamic acid dianion` (EXACT_SYNONYM). Both are names of the anion.
- `Sodium_Citrate` (dihydrate CHEBI:32142): its preferred term `Sodium Citrate` is a generic name, and its synonym `Na2citrate` names disodium citrate.

Suggested order:

1. Retype those names as REJECTED_LABEL, or move each to the record for its form, with curation events.
2. Set `representative:` on the nine tombstones. If review pins (#740, #745) block these edits, change claw instead: when looking for the merge, skip events whose `previous_status` is already REJECTED.
3. Rebuild with `just rebuild-unified`. Check that the 33 rows come back, except the 11 occurrences whose form has no record.
4. Add a gate. `check-unified-freshness` and `check-unified-rejections` both pass on the current snapshot. Either of these checks would have caught this:
   - every merge tombstone carries `representative:`;
   - no REJECTED row without an identity has a tombstone's name as its label.

Related:
- #878 covers MAPPED labels that sit on a different hydrate.
- #877 is the membership rebuild. It reports that CultureMech#591 now refuses tombstone redirects across hydrates on CultureMech's side.

## Correction to #863

#863's description calls rows like these "merged-tombstone answers that the reviewed builder withholds (MIM #811, #816)". Nothing is withheld on purpose: the builder loses the merge target as described above, and neither #811 nor #816 covers that.

items.title: Reground eight records onto the specific form their CAS names (#320)
items.body:
Applies the #320 curation decision: **where a record's CAS names a more specific *form* than its label — a salt, hydrate or racemate — the CAS governs**, on the reading that the recipe means the substance actually weighed out.

These surfaced as "unrelated" in the ancestry triage only because **ChEBI does not model salt-of / hydrate-of / racemate-of as subsumption** — the same modelling gap #342 recorded for hydrates, and the reason the descendant test couldn't classify them either way.

| record | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| `Carboxymethyl cellulose` | `CHEBI:85146` carboxymethylcellulose | `CHEBI:234035` **sodium salt** |
| `Mg-citrate` | `CHEBI:131389` magnesium citrate | `CHEBI:131391` **trimagnesium dicitrate** |
| `1,2-Dichloropropane` | `CHEBI:142468` | `CHEBI:82163` **rac-** |
| `alpha-Lactose` | `CHEBI:36219` alpha-lactose | `CHEBI:189432` **monohydrate** |
| `Berberine` | `CHEBI:16118` berberine | `CHEBI:31271` **chloride** |
| `Kawain` | `CHEBI:6117` Kawain | `CHEBI:156288` **DL-kavain** |
| `Meropenem` | `CHEBI:43968` meropenem | `CHEBI:6770` **trihydrate** |

`Sodium Citrate` is a **merge**, not a regrounding — its CAS `6132-04-3` denotes the dihydrate and `Na3-citrate x 2 H2O` already holds `CHEBI:32142`. Occurrences 65 + 11 → 76.

## One record deliberately excluded

**`Thiamine pyrophosphate`** does *not* fall under this decision. Its CAS `136-09-4` points to `CHEBI:45931 thiamine(1+) diphosphate(1-)`, whose ChEBI definition is *"the **conjugate base** of thiamine(1+) diphosphate"* — a **charge state**, not a salt, hydrate or stereo form. #319's protonation rule governs it, so the `CHEBI:9532` mapping from #351 stands.

Five others (`Malate`, `3-Hydroxypropionate`, `DL-carnitine`, `phosphorous acid`, `N-Acetyl-L-glutamine`) were already adjudicated correct under #319 and are untouched.

## Verification

SSSOM Rules A/B1/B2/B3 · reconcile 0 gap/orphan/stale · roundtrip 0 errors · flat exports fresh · `validate-strict` 0 ERROR rows · 911 tests · duplicate baseline refreshed deliberately (1 GONE, 0 NEW) · #352 case-drift guard: 0.

items.title: Retire the residual #232 label conflicts: names of a different form
items.body:
Refs #758 (deferred behind #740).

Part of #232. After #732 and the four #312 batches the label index still reported **29** rows under `conflict:different_substances`. Every one is a synonym that names a different chemical form than the record it sits on, or is not a name at all. This retypes them `REJECTED_LABEL` (provenance only; they no longer resolve, export, or enter `other`).

| token | on | what it actually names |
|---|---|---|
| `cobalt(2+) chloride`, `cobalt(II) chloride` | CoCl2 x 2 H2O, x 4 H2O (local identities), x 6 H2O tombstone | the anhydrous CHEBI:35696, enriched when the hydrates still shared that term |
| `sodium phosphate monobasic anhydrous` | NaH2PO4 x 2 H2O | the anhydrous CHEBI:37585 |
| `sodium dioxido(dioxo)molybdenum` | Na2MoO4·2H2O tombstone | the anhydrous CHEBI:75215 |
| `trisodium 2-hydroxypropane-1,2,3-tricarboxylate` | Sodium_Citrate and Trisodium_Citrate_X_2_H2o tombstones (both CHEBI:32142 dihydrate) | anhydrous trisodium citrate CHEBI:53258 |
| `CaCl2 × 2 H2O`, `CaCl2*2H2O` | Calcium_Chloride tombstone (CHEBI:3312) | the dihydrate, Cacl2_X_2_H2o |
| `a-Ketoglutaric acid` | the disodium salt hydrate | the free acid record |
| `L-glutamate` | Na-glutamate tombstone | the anion |
| `Optional ingredient` | D-fructose, Cellulose, Na-acetate, CaCO3 | a CultureMech recipe annotation |

`scripts/retire_wrong_form_names.py` verifies each token at run time against `chebi.db` and the owning record before writing. 14 records (5 tombstones), 18 tokens, 8 SSSOM rows' `other` scrubbed. **Label-index conflicts 29 → 0.** The citrate identity questions in #704 are untouched: only names ChEBI assigns to a different form move.

Review chain: receipt `issue232-wrong-form-names` (sequence 5); dispositions unchanged (1751 / 1272), synonym-only change.

## Review findings

Filed: #758 (the dihydrate record carries three monohydrate spellings, and CultureMech counts their 36 recipes, plus 4 dihydrate-spelling recipes, under anhydrous NaH2PO4). The fix, `scripts/move_nah2po4_hydrate_labels.py`, was verified locally (NaH2PO4 237 → 197, dihydrate 53 → 57, monohydrate 50 → 86) but the count refresh on `Nah2po4.yaml` hits the identity-plan pin (#740), so it ships here with the blocker documented and is not applied.

## Checks run

All local gates OK (`validate-all`, `validate-products`, `qc-sssom`, `qc-flat-coverage`, `qc-roundtrip`, `qc-duplicate-ids`, `qc-kg-microbe-node-ids`, `qc-component-partonomy`, `qc-evidence`, `check-instruction-refs`, `check-curation-targets`); `reconcile_sssom.py` in sync; visualization currency OK; indexes regenerated; both review products exported and validated from clean output directories. Full `pytest tests/`: 2757 passed, 1 failed (`test_unified_freshness::test_the_committed_snapshot_is_within_budget`, the pre-existing unified drift budget; CI's shallow checkout skips it).

items.title: Stop calling merge targets thieves, and retire 30 synonyms that name other compounds (#669)
items.body:
Addresses #669 (115 → 59 baselined pairs) and fixes #698's rename path.

Rule K (#670) baselined 115 pairs where a row's `other` carried a name another record owns. Cleaning them meant asking *why* each was there. Three different answers came back.

## 1. 54 were never violations — my own rule was wrong

Rule K's ownership map read every file under `mapped/` without checking `mapping_status`. A `REJECTED` record there is a **merge tombstone**: 62 of the 63 in the corpus carry a MERGE-type event, and the last is an explicit `REPOINTED_TOMBSTONE_IDENTIFIER`. The merge moved the name to the target, so `MIM:Acetate` carrying `Acetate (carbon source)` is the rightful holder, not a thief.

Tombstones no longer own names. 51 false positives and 3 already-stale entries leave the baseline, and a new test refuses any baseline entry that matches no live violation — so it can only shrink honestly.

## 2. 40 of the remaining 61 are a harmless round trip

They arrive from kg-microbe's synonyms for the *shared ontology object*. Downstream they re-attach to that same object. Ugly in this file, harmless in the graph. Left baselined.

## 3. The other 21 are where the real problem was

`Ca(NO3)2` is **calcium** nitrate (`CHEBI:64205`). It was once mis-mapped to **cadmium** nitrate; the mapping was corrected, and the six synonyms harvested while it was wrong stayed behind. They publish through `other` on an `exactMatch` row, which kg-microbe merges into the object's synonym set.

In the label index CultureMech consumes:

```
-Cadmium(II) nitrate,synonym,CHEBI:64205,Ca(NO3)2,…,MAPPED,unique
-arsenite,synonym,CHEBI:29125,Arsenate,…,MAPPED,unique
```

Resolved **uniquely** — not even flagged ambiguous. Rule K saw one of the six, because only one happens to be another record's preferred_term.

So the sweep is by **ChEBI's own name lists**, not by Rule K: a synonym ChEBI gives to a different term and does *not* give to the record's own.

| record | carried names of | n |
|---|---|---:|
| Ca(NO3)2 *calcium nitrate* | **cadmium nitrate** | 6 |
| Arsenate | **arsenite(1−)** — different oxidation state | 6 |
| Lithocholic acid | tricine, berbaman | 4 |
| Thiamine pyrophosphate | **pyrithiamine pyrophosphate** — its antagonist | 3 |
| Na2S2O3 | nonaethylene glycol monomethyl ether | 3 |
| 3-Indolyl acetic acid / 4-Hydroxyphenyl acetic acid / DL-Malic acid | ethyl 2-hexenoate / aspyrone / garciniaxanthone F | 2 each |
| Phenyl acetic acid / Trisodium citrate | LSM-15166 / citric acid | 1 each |

**30 on 10 records.** Each (own, wrong) pair checked by hand: no ChEBI edge joins the two in either direction, and their InChIKey connectivity differs. Related forms — paraquat and its dichloride, a stereoisomer and its racemate — show a `has_part` edge or a shared skeleton, are a curator's call, and are **not** touched.

Marked `REJECTED_LABEL`, not deleted. The provenance is real, and claw's builder filters *every* candidate alternate — kg-microbe's included — through the record's rejected labels, so the tombstone keeps a name out even while kg-microbe still supplies it. Deletion would let the next rebuild restore it. All ten `other` cells match what claw's merged builder produces.

Twelve of the thirty carry the source `sssom_other_backfill` — a backfill copied SSSOM `other` tokens *back* into curated YAML, round-tripping kg-microbe's contamination into MIM's records.

## 4. Doing this by the book exposed a defect in the book — #698

`save_yaml` backs a file up into a **gitignored** `backups/` directory beside it. The exporter's filename index enumerated with `rglob`, so every edited record appeared twice, both continuity keys collided, `for_record` returned `None`, and **`just sync-curated` renamed the records that had just been edited**.

| checkout | records with no filename continuity |
|---|---:|
| pristine `main` | 0 |
| after this ten-record edit | **21 — 8 of them published SSSOM subjects** |

On macOS git cannot see it (`core.ignorecase`), but a local claw rebuild published `MIM:Ca_NO32` for `MIM:Ca_No32`. On a case-sensitive filesystem it strands the subject outright — the #236/#300 failure, arriving through the filesystem.

`iter_record_files()` now enumerates the way `aggregate_records` does. With 11 backups present, `sync-curated` re-cases **0** files, down from 8. My own freshness gate from #653 had the same `rglob` and takes the same fix. No field was lost on the ten records — checked key by key.

## Verification

Mutation-checked: restoring the `rglob` fails 3 tests; letting tombstones own names again fails 2.

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `validate-all` / `qc-sssom` (A–L) / `qc-roundtrip` / `qc-flat-coverage` / `check-unified-freshness` | pass |
| `lint` / `format-check` / `typecheck` / `check-instruction-refs` | clean |

`sync-curated` also corrected `mapped_count`, already stale on `main` (2618 declared, 2616 actual). No record's status moved here.

items.title: Resolve four CAS-vs-CURIE conflicts; 48 of the 84 are not defects (#320)
items.body:
> **Stacked on #341.** Base is `curation/hydrate-registry-terms`; retarget to `main` once #341 merges.

## The main result: 48 of 84 are not defects

#320's check asks whether a record's `cas_rn` is registered by ChEBI against a *different* term than the record's CURIE. That conflates two situations, separable with one query — **is the CAS's term a descendant of the record's term?**

| relationship | count | reading |
|---|---|---|
| CAS's term is a **descendant** | **48** | CAS is finer-grained than a deliberately generic term — expected |
| CAS's term is an **ancestor** | 3 | CURIE over-specific for the label |
| CAS's term is **unrelated** | 33 | genuine conflict |

The 48 are the `Arginine` → `CHEBI:29016 arginine`, CAS `74-79-3` → `L-arginine` shape (also `Ascorbic acid`, `D-Ribose`, `D-Mannose`, `caffeic acid`, `Anethole`). The label matches the generic term *exactly*, §3 step 4 makes that term correct, and the CAS registry has no number for a stereo-unspecified class.

This explains why the heuristics recorded in #338 kept failing: 23 of the 84 sit on structureless class terms, but structurelessness cuts across **all three** rows, so it can never discriminate. Ancestry does.

## Four conflicts resolved — and they were duplicates

The root cause from #315/#334 again: **the CAS conflict is a symptom of a duplicate record, not a bad mapping.** ChEBI has the right term, the record's own CAS points at it, and another MIM record already holds it under the correct name.

| record | was | now | winner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `m-Inositol` | `CHEBI:10642` scyllo-inositol | `CHEBI:17268` | `myo-Inositol` |
| `NiSO4 x 6 H2O` | `CHEBI:53001` nickel sulfate | `CHEBI:53437` | `Nickel (II) sulfate hexahydrate` |
| `maltose` | `CHEBI:18167` alpha-maltose | `CHEBI:17306` | `Maltose` |

`m-Inositol` is the sharpest — it *is* myo-inositol, grounded to a different stereoisomer by a `CAS_RN_LOOKUP` that its own CAS `87-89-8` contradicts. `maltose` differs from `Maltose` only in the case of one letter.

`Sodium succinate dibasic` is `cas:`-primary, so the script's identifier guard **refused to merge it** — the guard working as designed. Its parent moves instead: `CHEBI:15741 succinic acid` → `CHEBI:63675 sodium succinate`, whose `C4H4O4.2Na` is the dibasic salt the label names. It stays cas-primary per §3 step 2.

## Deliberately not touched

- **`Dextrose`** — its CAS resolves to three terms (`glucose`, `D-glucose`, `aldehydo-D-glucose`), each already held by a *different* MIM record (`Glucose`, `D-Glucose`, `glucose`). A four-way tangle; picking one winner piecemeal would prejudge it.
- **`N-Acetyl-L-glutamine`** — its own term matches the label exactly and the CAS's term is the stereo-unspecified ancestor, so §3 step 4 makes the current mapping right. Merging would lose the L-.

## Verification

SSSOM Rules A/B1/B2/B3 pass · reconcile 0 gap/orphan/stale · roundtrip 0 errors · flat exports fresh · 880 tests pass · duplicate baseline refreshed deliberately (1 GONE, 0 NEW).

Residual on #320: **84 → 80**, of which 48 are now identified as non-defects, leaving **32** genuine candidates.

items.title: Move the SSSOM surface forms only MIM knows onto the records (#520)
items.body:
Implements the decision recorded on #520: **ontology synonyms are curated onto records,
not emitted by the builder.**

## Why not the builder

kg-microbe transforms ChEBI itself — 158,214 of 200,000 sampled nodes carry synonyms —
and for `CHEBI:16004` its node holds a **superset** of MIM's row. So **7,713** of the
tokens a rebuild drops are a second, stale copy of data the consumer already has.
Emitting them from the builder would institutionalise that redundancy and leave MIM
shipping a ChEBI snapshot it cannot keep current.

MIM's unique contribution is the surface forms no ontology has (`n-propyl chloride`,
`1,2-propandiol`). **Only MIM sees the recipes**, so only a record can hold them. The
curation layer already assumes this — the builder honours
`NON_PUBLISHABLE_MIM_SYNONYM_TYPES = {"REJECTED_LABEL"}`, which only makes sense if
records are the source.

## What this lands

**114 surface forms onto 114 records** as `RAW_TEXT` (raw forms from an artifact whose
per-token provenance can't be verified; `EXACT_SYNONYM` would overstate them).

Effect on the published index: **+103 rows, all `unique`, conflicts unchanged at 468.**

## The guard is the point, and the first cut didn't have it

Adding a synonym is only safe if no *other* record already answers to that name.
`label_index.csv` is what CultureMech resolves against and it **fails closed** on a name
two records claim. Many ontology synonyms are legitimately shared across a family —
`L-aspartic acid` belongs to the acid, its potassium salt and its sodium salt alike.

Migrating 1,713 tokens without that check measured as:

| | unique | conflict:different_substances |
|---|---:|---:|
| `origin/main` | 8,758 | 468 |
| unguarded backfill | **8,271** | **1,921** |
| this PR | **8,861** | **468** |

The unguarded version would have made ~487 previously resolvable labels **unresolvable** —
strictly worse than the missing synonyms it set out to fix. 195 tokens are now skipped on
those grounds.

## Also deliberately not migrated

- **20 damaged forms whose repair reproduces a name already published.** `L--Aspartic
  acid`, `2--Mercaptoethanol`, `myo--Inositol` all collapse onto names the record *and*
  the kg-microbe node already carry, so they add nothing. Repair-then-retest is what
  shows this; a blanket drop was right for them only by accident.
- **6 role-text leaks** (`utilizes: 1,2-propandiol`, `carbon source: acetate`) — defects
  sitting in the published artifact, not synonyms.
- **1 truncated inside a parenthetical** — unrepairable without fabricating text.
  Unbalanced parentheses are the test.
- **1,409 tokens on 19 subjects whose record was renamed after publication** — filed as
  #523; they cannot be attributed to a current record.

## Two survivors were never damaged

`beta-D-glucopyranose, 4-O-beta-D-galactopyranosyl-` is CAS index nomenclature ending on
the substituent's hyphen, and ChEBI writes hydrates as `<compound>--water (1/n)`. My
first damage filter read both as truncation and discarded valid labels for the citrate,
cobalt-sulfate and phosphate hydrates.
